items.title: Govt stalls Alipay+ tie-up over data security concerns
items.description: Alipay+'s proposal to link with India's payment system faces national security concerns.  Concerns also exist regarding the storage and use of customer data.  This proposal was the first from a China-linked entity in the financial sector.  India and China are working to maintain peace at the border.  Chinese President Xi Jinping's visit is expected to stabilize bilateral relations.

items.title: Canara Bank eyes $2 billion overseas bond raise
items.description: Canara Bank plans to raise up to $2 billion from overseas markets under its MTN programme, with the funds to be mobilised through its GIFT City or other overseas branches.

items.title: Sebi set to review derivative settlement prices amid concerns over CAS
items.description: Sebi will review derivative settlement price methods.  This follows market participant feedback after the new closing auction session.  The regulator introduced the closing auction session in the equity cash segment.  This session determines the closing price of securities for derivatives.  A consultation paper on proposed changes will be issued soon.

items.title: FPIs pump Rs 13,010 crore into Indian equities in second half of August
items.description: Overseas investors continued buying Indian equities for five straight fortnights. They invested over thirteen thousand crore rupees in the latter half of August. Consumer services, financials, and healthcare sectors received significant foreign portfolio inflows. Capital goods also saw renewed investor interest after previous outflows. Oil, gas, and consumable fuels experienced the largest foreign investment outflows.

items.title: Pre-market action: Here's the trade setup for today's session
items.description: Domestic equities closed mixed as the Nifty saw a slight decline. Elevated crude oil prices are keeping investor sentiment cautious in the market. Foreign portfolio investors were net sellers, while domestic investors bought shares. The Indian Rupee continued its gaining momentum against the US dollar. Several stocks are currently under the F&O ban period.

items.title: Stocks in news: HDFC Bank, M&M, Gland Pharma, CreditAccess Grameen and Bharat Forge
items.description: Indian benchmark indices extended their losing streak for a fourth consecutive session on Thursday.  Nifty 50 fell 0.17% and Sensex declined 0.55% amid market pressures.  HDFC Bank raised nearly $12 billion through Foreign Currency Non-Resident deposits.  Mahindra & Mahindra expects truck business integration by January and electric bus launch by April.  Fosun Pharma is likely to divest a 5% stake in Gland Pharma through a block deal.

items.title: NSE’s mega IPO moves closer as SC approves Sebi settlement
items.description: In a pivotal decision, the Supreme Court has validated the National Stock Exchange’s settlement concerning the co-location and dark fibre matters. This marks a crucial step forward as the exchange readies for its initial public offering, expected to attract nearly thirty-one thousand crore rupees. Once completed, this IPO could become the second-largest in the nation, following the regulatory body’s acceptance of the significant settlement payment.

items.title: These large- and mid-cap stocks can give more than 20% return in 1 year, according to analysts
items.description: The Indian market was under pressure on Thursday, particularly at the index level. Rising crude-oil prices are an obvious concern, but domestic factors like selling and market repricing in select sectors may also be beginning to impact sentiment. Also, are there early indications that Indian equities will be charting their own course as compared to what is happening in the global markets?

items.title: Banks offer semi-fixed loans to deploy surplus liquidity
items.description: Banks are deploying surplus liquidity through new mortgage products.  HSBC and Kotak Mahindra Bank lead with semi-fixed home loan options.  These products offer fixed rates for a period before switching.  This strategy aims to protect lending margins amid interest rate uncertainty.  Surplus funds are also being considered for government securities.

items.title: LCR reset creates ₹2.1 Lakh-crore lending headroom for PSU Banks
items.description: Public sector banks gained significant lending headroom after liquidity requirement relaxation. This allows them to sustain credit growth while deposit mobilisation remains relatively weak. Excess investment buffers could support incremental loan growth on their substantial loan books. Banks can now free up funds tied up in government bonds for lending. This improvement is visible at some of the largest state-owned lenders.

items.title: IFCI shares rally 6% as NSE IPO buzz lifts sentiment; stock gains 35% in a month
items.description: IFCI Share Price: IFCI shares surged over 6% as optimism around the long-awaited NSE IPO boosted investor interest in the state-owned financial services company, which indirectly holds more than 4% of NSE through SHCIL. The stock has rallied nearly 35% in a month, while NSE’s potential IPO valuation and regulatory risks remain key factors for investors.

items.title: Gold prices fall Rs 2,100/10 gram after 2 days; silver down Rs 1,500/kg ahead of US payrolls data. Important levels for today
items.description: Following a brief rally, gold and silver prices opened lower on Friday, sparking caution among investors. The market is now focused on the US payrolls report, which may provide insights into Federal Reserve interest rate decisions. Geopolitical concerns in the Middle East are another pivotal factor affecting prices. Experts warn of potential volatility in the precious metals market and recommend long-term investment strategies.

items.title: Eternal, ICICI Bank, 5 other largecap stocks with upside potential of up to 40%. Do you own any?
items.description: Axis Securities has raised its December 2026 Nifty target to 27,360 as it remains constructive on Indian equities, supported by strong macroeconomic fundamentals, sustained government capital expenditure, GST 2.0 reforms and an improving corporate earnings cycle. Axis expects Nifty earnings to grow at a 13% CAGR over FY23-FY28, which it believes will underpin healthy medium-term market returns. Here are 7 largecap stocks that the brokerage is bullish on:

items.title: ESDS Software shares skyrocket 112% from IPO price as stock soars 20% after bumper debut. Should you buy, sell or wait?
items.description: ESDS Share Price: ESDS Software Solution shares more than doubled from their IPO price shortly after listing, hitting the 20% upper circuit following a blockbuster debut. With the stock’s sharp gains pushing valuations higher, analysts have outlined strategies for IPO allottees and investors who missed the issue, including profit-booking and entry levels.

items.title: Sterlite Tech shares hit 5% upper circuit as firm targets Rs 20,000 crore revenue by FY29 amid booming AI demand
items.description: Sterlite Technologies shares hit a 5% upper circuit after unveiling ambitious FY29 growth targets, including Rs 20,000 crore revenue and global top-five positioning. The company approved Rs 3,000 crore capex to expand capacity by 50%, supported by strong optical connectivity demand, AI infrastructure growth and a record order book.

items.title: PhysicsWallah shares surge over 4% after Motilal Oswal initiates coverage with Buy rating. Should you buy?
items.description: PhysicsWallah shares surged over 4% after Motilal Oswal initiated coverage with a ‘Buy’ rating and a Rs 200 target price, implying about 66% upside. The brokerage highlighted the company’s capital-efficient model, strong online presence and scalable offline network, while projecting revenue and EBITDA growth through FY28 and flagging competition, execution and AI-related risks.

items.title: IEX shares rise 2% after electricity trading volume jumps 20% YoY to hit record high in August
items.description: IEX shares rose on Friday after the exchange reported record monthly electricity trading volume of 13,938 MUs in August, up 20.2% year-on-year. Higher power demand lifted Day-Ahead Market buy bids, while prices also increased. However, REC volumes fell sharply amid lower participation, declining 86.6% year-on-year during the month.

items.title: Ceigall India shares gain 4% after securing LoI for Rs 5,300 crore power transmission project
items.description: Ceigall India shares rose nearly 4% after the company received a Letter of Intent from REC Power Development and Consultancy for a Rs 5,300 crore power transmission project in Gujarat. The project includes a 765/400 kV AIS substation and around 300 km of transmission lines, with 36 months of execution followed by a 35-year operational period and annual transmission charges of Rs 608.67 crore.

items.title: BSE, Groww, Angel One shares rally up to 8% after Sebi’s CAS circular. What did the regulator say?
items.description: Sebi plans to review the methodology for setting derivative settlement prices on expiry after market participants raised concerns over the new Closing Auction Session (CAS). The regulator will issue a consultation paper next week.

items.title: Polycab, KEI Industries shares crash up to 9% after UltraTech Cement enters wires & cables business. What Jefferies, Nuvama expect
items.description: Shares of Polycab and KEI Industries fell sharply after UltraTech Cement launched its ₹1,800 crore wires and cables business, Ultravolt. Brokerages warned that the Aditya Birla Group’s aggressive entry could trigger near-term de-rating across the cables and wires sector, although Nuvama retained Polycab and KEI as its top picks.

items.title: Large trade alert! Gland Pharma shares fall 3% after 1.2 crore shares change hands in 2 block deals; promoter Fosun likely seller
items.description: Gland Pharma shares fell 3% after 1.22 crore shares changed hands in two block deals worth nearly Rs 5,818 crore. Promoter Fosun Pharma Industrial was reportedly looking to sell a 5% stake for Rs 2,279.5 crore. Meanwhile, the company’s recent USFDA inspection of two Visakhapatnam facilities concluded with zero Form 483 observations.

items.title: Sensex climbs 600 points, but Nifty gains marginally. What lies ahead?
items.description: The Indian stock market opened with a sharp divergence on Friday. The Sensex rose around 0.7% while the Nifty posted only marginal gains. Broader markets also opened in the green, with Nifty Midcap 100 recording slight gains. Bajaj Finserv shares led gains on Sensex, rising around two percent. The overall market breadth was positive, showing more advances than declines.

items.title: HAL shares rise nearly 3% as GE Aerospace delivers 3 more F404 engines for Tejas Mk1A
items.description: HAL shares rose nearly 3% after GE Aerospace delivered three F404-IN20 engines in August for India’s LCA Tejas Mk1A programme. The deliveries come amid prolonged supply delays, as HAL works to fulfil Indian Air Force orders for 180 Mk1A fighters. HAL currently has an annual production capacity of 24 aircraft, with engine supplies critical to ramping up production.

items.title: Tata Chemicals shares fall 3% after Kenya orders end to operations. Here’s why
items.description: Tata Chemicals reported a consolidated net loss of Rs 17 crore in the June 2026 quarter, compared with a profit of Rs 252 crore a year earlier. Revenue rose 14.4% to Rs 4,255 crore, supported by higher volumes, but EBITDA fell 14.5% amid weaker overseas realisations. Shares have declined 15% in 2026 and over 30% in the past year.

items.title: Reliance shares are down 17% despite soaring refining margins. What the market is missing
items.description: Despite strong refining and petrochemical margins, Reliance shares have experienced a dip as the market focuses on long-term growth potential. Investors are keenly anticipating signs of recovery in Reliance Retail and progress in New Energy initiatives. A significant concern remains the company's capability to generate free cash flow, with analysts indicating that the stock's valuation is closely tied to its future business performance.

items.title: ​Finolex Cables among 4 stocks flashing bullish signals, hinting at a possible uptrend
items.description: On September 3, four stocks in the Nifty500 appeared on the ‘White Marubozu’ bullish scanner, according to StockEdge’s technical scan data. A White Marubozu is a bullish candlestick pattern in technical analysis that occurs when the opening price is the lowest for a given period and the closing price is the highest. Represented by a long white (or green) candlestick with no upper shadow and a small or nonexistent lower shadow, it indicates strong buying pressure throughout the session. Traders interpret it as a signal that buyers were in control from the opening to the closing, often using such patterns for informed decisions about future price movements in financial markets.

items.title: Bumper FCNR(B) inflows may dilute banks' margins but boost earnings by up to Rs 11,000 crore: Jefferies
items.description: The FCNR(B) scheme’s $127 billion inflows should boost banking sector earnings by Rs 10,000–11,000 crore annually, despite potential near-term margin pressure. Analysts highlight significant benefits for small private banks and NBFCs, while providing the RBI with increased foreign exchange reserves.

items.title: Ola Electric shares gain 4% as EV maker rolls out first dealer-led stores
items.description: Ola Electric shares rose nearly 4% after the EV maker launched its first dealer-led stores across seven states. The move comes a month after opening its sales and service network to partners. Ola Electric plans to expand to more than 500 dealerships over the next couple of quarters to strengthen its retail presence.

items.title: Retail investors raise stakes in 10 stocks for two straight quarters; shares rally up to 80% in CY26
items.description: Shareholding data for the June 2026 quarter show that retail investors raised their stakes in 98 BSE 500 companies for a second straight quarter, extending the trend through June 2026. This points to rising confidence among individual investors. Retail investors include resident individuals holding nominal share capital of up to Rs 2 lakh.However, the increase in retail ownership has not resulted in broad-based gains across the BSE 500 universe. Stock performance has remained largely muted so far in CY26, with only about 23 companies posting positive returns. Still, despite the wider market weakness, a select group of stocks has stood out. Here are 10 BSE 500 stocks that have rallied between 20% and 80% in CY26 so far. (Data Source: ACE Equity)

items.title: Market chaos after CAS: What exactly is Sebi reviewing and will it stop expiry-day wild swings?
items.description: Sebi’s review of derivative settlement price methodology could reduce sharp expiry-day swings linked to the Closing Auction Session (CAS). Analysts expect the regulator to consider delinking derivative settlements from CAS closing prices rather than scrapping the mechanism. However, a revised framework may curb extreme volatility without eliminating normal expiry-day market swings.

items.title: Sebi moves ahead with action against Hindenburg, others in Adani case: Report
items.description: Sebi has started hearing representations as it seeks to recover gains from trades it suspects were based on prior knowledge of Hindenburg Research’s 2023 report on the Adani Group. The regulator had alleged that Kingdon Capital built short positions in Adani-related stocks before the report triggered a selloff, wiping out $150 billion in group value. Adani denied wrongdoing.

items.title: Will BDL, HAL & other defence stocks deliver rocketing returns? Here’s why this brokerage remains bullish
items.description: India’s defence sector is gaining momentum on the back of rising defence spending, localisation, strong order pipelines and growing exports. Bajaj Broking remains bullish on Bharat Dynamics and Hindustan Aeronautics, citing improving execution, robust order books and long-term military modernisation as key growth drivers.

items.title: Value stocks are making a comeback in India. These 10 stocks could benefit
items.description: India’s value-stock universe is showing signs of recovery after a sharp decline during the previous bull run. ICICI Securities has identified 10 stocks, led by Vedanta, ONGC and Indian Oil, that meet its value criteria based on earnings yield, return on equity, valuations, earnings trends and potential catalysts.

items.title: JM Financial initiates coverage on OnEMI Technology with Buy call, sees 28% upside
items.description: JM Financial has initiated coverage on OnEMI Technology Solutions with a Buy rating and a target price of Rs 385, implying around 28% upside from its reference price of Rs 301. The brokerage values the stock at 2x estimated FY28 book value, citing its digital lending platform Kissht and mass-market borrower focus.

items.title: Is AI boom hiding growing US risks? Nomura warns dollar asset concentration leaves global markets vulnerable to AI shocks
items.description: Nomura warned that the AI boom may be masking growing US risks, as heavy global exposure to dollar assets leaves markets vulnerable to an AI-driven shock. The brokerage said a setback in AI could trigger a sharp correction in US equities, weaken the dollar and potentially turn into a broader global risk-off event.

items.title: Which stocks should you buy ahead of the festive season? Here are Kotak Securities’ top 10 picks
items.description: India’s festive season is expected to drive a strong consumption boost, with analysts identifying sectors and stocks that could benefit. The period from Ganesh Chaturthi through Navratri, Dussehra, Dhanteras, Diwali and the wedding season typically brings higher footfalls, orders, ticket sizes and margins.

items.title: Swiggy sees 4% equity change hands in block deals; shares gain 2.5%
items.description: Swiggy shares rose 2.53% following block deals involving 4% equity. The company faces MSCI index removal on September 7 due to foreign ownership caps, while Q1 FY27 results showed a narrowed net loss of Rs 791 crore.

items.title: Sudeep Pharma among 8 commodities stocks hitting 52-week highs; rallied up to 55% in a month
items.description: Benchmark Sensex rose 363 points to close at 76,515. During the rally, eight stocks from the BSE Commodities Index touched fresh 52-week highs, their highest levels in the past year. A 52-week high simply indicates that a stock has reached its highest price level in the last year and may reflect increased market activity and investor interest.

items.title: Sebi, European Markets Authority partner for cooperation on central counterparties
items.description: Sebi and the European Securities and Markets Authority (ESMA) signed a memorandum of understanding to enhance cooperation and information exchange regarding central counterparties. This agreement replaces the 2017 pact, facilitating safer cross-border clearing and market infrastructure regulation.

items.title: Market wrap:  RIL,Tata Steel, Bharti Airtel, HCL Tech top gainers and losers on Nifty and Sensex on Friday
items.description: Indian equity markets ended Friday with a relief rally, led by metal and banking stocks, as concerns over an imminent US Fed rate hike eased. Nifty gained 0.1%, while Sensex rose 0.48%. SBI Life and Tata Steel were among the top gainers, while HCL Tech and Bharti Airtel declined.

items.title: Stock picks of the week: 6 stocks with consistent score improvement and an upside potential of up to 17%
items.description: You might ask: Why does it matter to India? In actual fact, it matters not only to India, but to the whole world. Yes, we are talking of an increase in US interest rates. It can change the whole global inflows equation. Our selected stocks for today depict a strong upward trajectory in their overall average score which is based on five key pillars: Earnings, fundamentals, relative valuation, risk, and price momentum. This implies that there has been a significant improvement in their market outlook in the given time frame.

items.title: Gland Pharma block deal: Fosun Pharma divests 99 lakh shares worth Rs 2,800 crore
items.description: Fosun Pharma sold a 6% stake in Gland Pharma for ₹2,800 crore via a block deal, reducing its holding to 45.77%. Major buyers included Kotak, Axis, and ICICI Prudential Mutual Funds, while Gland Pharma shares closed higher at ₹2,932.40.
